name: Takpenes
title: Egyptian Queen and Hadad's Mother-in-Law
summary: Takpenes was an Egyptian queen, wife of the pharaoh, who lived during Solomon's time. She is known for giving her sister in marriage to Hadad from Edom, an enemy of Solomon. She also raised her sister's son Genubath in the house of Pharaoh.

keyEvents.title: Hadad Flees to Egypt
keyEvents.description: After Joab had defeated the Edomites, the young Hadad fled to Egypt, where the pharaoh welcomed him and gave him land, food, and a house.

keyEvents.title: Takpenes' Sister Given to Hadad
keyEvents.description: The pharaoh gave Hadad the sister of his queen Takpenes as a wife, which showed the high status Hadad received at the Egyptian court.

keyEvents.title: Genubath's Birth and Upbringing
keyEvents.description: Takpenes' sister gave birth to a son named Genubath, whom Takpenes raised in the house of Pharaoh among Pharaoh's own sons.

keyEvents.title: Hadad Becomes an Adversary of Solomon
keyEvents.description: After Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he asked the pharaoh for permission to return to his own land, where he became an adversary of Solomon as God's judgment on Solomon's apostasy.
